headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks arise from MinerU’s MCP/file ingestion feeding Plane’s broad-network task workflows; compliance and leakage are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can ingest local documents and exposes an MCP Server, so attacker-controlled file content could reach Plane if Plane consumes MinerU outputs or shared files. Plane’s file uploads and issue/task surfaces make instruction-like content plausible. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plane ingests MinerU-produced text or OCR output as instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or MCP workflow, attacker-controlled document content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on MinerU output.
Add provenance tags to all MinerU exports before Plane imports them.
Require human review for any task created from extracted document text.
Restrict Plane imports to sanitized, non-executable summaries.
requires-engineering: add content-type and trust-boundary enforcement between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while Plane has broad network egress and file uploads. A leakage path exists if sensitive documents processed by MinerU are uploaded into Plane, but the profiles do not show shared storage or automatic syncing. That makes the blast radius limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs or OCR text are uploaded from MinerU into Plane, those contents may leave the local boundary.
IF Plane is used with external network access on imported files, document data can be exposed beyond the original workspace.
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a local-only directory.
Do not upload extracted documents into Plane unless redacted.
Use a separate workspace for sensitive files.
Review Plane file-upload permissions before importing outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on MinerU-to-Plane transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU has no filesystem write, no shell, and no git modification; Plane also has no filesystem write and no git state access. The pair therefore lacks the overlapping mutable capabilities that would create a serious write conflict. Uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly show no shared write surface.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF Plane is extended with filesystem-write plugins, overlapping mutation could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only to shared locations.
Separate their working directories.
Avoid granting git or database write scopes to either agent.
Check orchestrator permissions before co-running them.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR that Plane could plausibly turn into issues or schedules. Plane’s task-oriented workflow can act on that output, so a mistaken extraction can cascade into incorrect tickets or plans. The profiles do not prove direct automation, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Plane creates issues or schedules directly from MinerU extraction without verification, errors will propagate.
IF OCR or table extraction is wrong and Plane treats it as authoritative, downstream work products become incorrect.
mitigations: Require human verification before creating Plane items from MinerU output.
Attach source-document links to every imported task.
Use confidence thresholds for extracted fields.
Sample-check a few extracted records before bulk import.
requires-engineering: add validation rules between extraction and task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while Plane is self-hosted deployable but also has broad network egress and external contact surfaces. A compliance mismatch can occur if regulated documents are moved from the offline MinerU boundary into Plane’s networked environment, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated documents processed by MinerU are transferred into a Plane deployment with external network access, residency or retention obligations may be affected.
IF Plane’s retention or logging differs from the local MinerU workflow, compliance gaps can appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data in the offline MinerU workflow.
Confirm Plane retention settings before importing sensitive files.
Use a separate tenant or deployment for regulated content.
Document the data flow for audits.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems.
